### 📓 Docs Drift Check
Nothing in this diff resolved to a documentable surface (no symbol, route or SDK anchor derived from **0** changed package(s)), so **this run has no opinion** about the docs.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **0** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 4443014630c094cde840f9dd0b0b45ade45b48d9` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## 席位核对

**L1 review · ACCEPT** · Head-sha: `5a699ff727251ea5e61c851a524878d79ab53546` · card #34834 · read 2026-11-17T23:24Z

This is a full review: there is no earlier L1 record. The PR is one commit on merge-base `44430146` that changes one file, `packages/lint/src/validate-expressions.flow-null-guards.test.ts` (+9 / -4). I also read the card, triage 6948468020, the claim and the body.

- **Surface:** it is the claimed file only. No timeout was raised, nothing was skipped or quarantined, and no test was deleted.
- **The change:** the three-tier loop moves from inside one `it` to around it. Each generated `it` holds the old loop body, byte for byte at the same indentation. All three tiers, all six columns and all five sites are still asserted with the same `expect(build, …).toEqual(atDoor(…))`. The suite goes from 29 to 31 tests, as reported.
- **Is splitting a fix, or a way around the cap? It is a fix.** The 5 s cap is a budget for each claim, and the three tiers were always three independent claims: each builds its own `tiered` stack and its own `servedTier`, and none reads another's state. Folded together, they spent three claims' worth of time against one claim's budget. After the split, each case costs what its untiered sibling at line 433 costs (about 0.2 s idle), and that sibling was already within the cap in the same leg. The card forbids narrowing, skipping or deleting the check. Nothing here does any of those.
- **Triage's direction was checked, not just set aside.** Triage suggested hoisting a booted fixture, but the case boots none. The body's profile puts the build-side cost in `runAuthoringRules('build')` (about 6.3 ms per call). Every (tier, column, site) input is distinct, so nothing can be shared. Batching sites into one stack would change the `flows[k]` path that the build-equals-door comparison reads. The new code comment states the reason, with the numbers.
- **Names:** no other file in the tree cites the old case title, so no ledger or doc goes stale.
- **Changeset:** skipping it is right, since `@objectstack/lint` publishes `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md` only. Clause-② is `no` and Metadata-protocol is `none`, which fit a test-only diff. The PR is not governed.
- **Closing keyword:** `Closes #34834` is consistent with the card's workflow. A closed card is never reopened, and a later red is filed fresh. The 20:03Z scheduled run (`44165198824`, `44c7a4a4`) was already green, which confirms the case was a load-timed overrun and not a deterministic failure. The split adds margin for the next loaded run.
- **Gates at this head (latest attempt per check):** none failed so far (17 success, 11 skipped, 36 still running).

### Nit

- **N1: the real cost lever has no carrier.** The body records the per-call re-read of the spec liveness ledgers (`lintLivenessProperties` → `loadWarnMap`, about 55% of a build call) as "Noted, not filed · carrier: none". That cost lands on every suite that calls `runAuthoringRules('build')` many times, so it is the next load-timed red waiting to happen. Please file it as a finding on the triage mailbox, so the lever outlives this card. It is production code outside this card's surface, and it does not block this PR.

**Owed:** nothing from the seat beyond landing on green. There is no contract face: the diff is test-only. This comment readies, queues and arms nothing.
